questions.stem: In which established class of systems is the conceptual foundation of Lakebase rooted?
questions.explanation: Lakebase's conceptual foundation is rooted in HTAP systems, which emerged to break the divide between OLTP and OLAP within a single environment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the modernised architectural elements that Lakebase introduces?
options: AI-native compatibility and elastic serverless scaling
questions.explanation: Lakebase decouples compute from storage; tight compute-storage coupling is a limitation of traditional HTAP that Lakebase addresses.

questions.stem: Which three siloed tool categories are described as having shackled enterprises for decades before Lakebase?
options: OLTP systems for transactions, OLAP platforms for analytics and AI/ML stacks operating in isolation
Data marts, data warehouses and data lakes
questions.explanation: Enterprises were shackled by OLTP systems for transactions, OLAP platforms for analytics and isolated AI/ML stacks, causing latency, duplication and governance breakdowns.

questions.stem: What storage does Lakebase use, in contrast to the proprietary or row-store storage of traditional HTAP?
questions.explanation: Lakebase stores data in Delta Tables, which are columnar and transactional, whereas traditional HTAP relied on proprietary or row-store storage.

questions.stem: How is governance handled in Lakebase, compared with traditional HTAP?
options: Governance is left to each application
Governance is handled by manual spreadsheets
Governance is metadata-first via Unity Catalog
questions.explanation: Traditional HTAP governance is limited and engine-bound; Lakebase is metadata-first, with governance handled via Unity Catalog.

questions.stem: What does Lakebase transform metadata into?
options: An active, decision-making layer rather than passive documentation
questions.explanation: Lakebase transforms metadata from passive documentation into an active, decision-making layer, making metadata the control plane.

questions.stem: In the Lakebase architectural flow, what API does the application use to connect?
questions.explanation: In the Lakebase flow, the application connects through a Postgres-compatible API to decoupled compute and Delta Table storage.

questions.stem: In the FinTech fraud detection comparison, which components did the Lakebase approach use?
options: TiDB for ingestion and a local cache
Branch-per-session design for scoring, PgVector for embeddings, Delta Lake for storage and Unity Catalog for governance and lineage
questions.explanation: The Lakebase approach leveraged branch-per-session scoring, PgVector embeddings, Delta Lake storage and Unity Catalog governance, yielding elastic inference and auditability.

questions.stem: In the telecom data monetisation example, what outcome followed the upgrade from SAP HANA to Lakebase?
options: A 30% cost reduction and improved service agility
The removal of all AI capabilities
questions.explanation: Switching to disaggregated compute with Delta Lake and AI API layers produced a 30% cost reduction and improved service agility.

questions.stem: Which statement reflects why Lakebase matters as businesses move toward federated data platforms and autonomous systems?
options: Metadata should be ignored in favour of raw data
Workloads should each have their own separate source of truth
Analytics and transactions must remain in separate systems
Metadata is the control plane, real-time agents require rollback-ready snapshots, and workloads span dashboards, models, APIs and pipelines from a single source of truth
questions.explanation: The shifted architectural needs are that metadata is the control plane, real-time agents need rollback-ready snapshots, and all workloads draw from a single source of truth.
